plan.audience: Mostly local Bay Area adults aged about 25-54: San Francisco and East Bay Warriors fans, young professionals, some families, plus a small group of Kings fans who mostly drive from Sacramento. On a weeknight, many come straight from downtown San Francisco offices by walking or by Muni. East Bay fans tend to take BART into Embarcadero or Powell and then Muni, walk or ride-hail; others drive to Mission Bay garages or use ride-hail.
plan.attendance_reason: The cited source says Warriors home games sell out Chase Center's 18,064 seats, and demand is rated sold_out. Attendance is capped at capacity. A few no-shows are possible on the day before Thanksgiving, but they are not enough to lower the figure.
plan.reference_reason: This is the only measured reference at the same station. Like Oracle Park, it is a San Francisco professional night event with Muni, Caltrain and ferry competition and a walk or transfer from Embarcadero. Chase Center is about 1.5 km further south in Mission Bay, so access from Embarcadero is clearly worse than the Oracle Park reference.
multiplier_reasons: Parking: the Mission Bay garages around Chase Center give roughly as much or slightly more parking than at Oracle Park, so there is a small downward effect. The size is uncertain; the specialist's claim of clearly more parking is softened.

Crowd type: NBA crowds pay higher ticket prices and lean more toward ride-hail and driving than Giants crowds. There is a modest downward effect, partly offset because Warriors fans are heavily local, including East Bay commuters.

plan.end_reason: A regulation NBA game from a 19:00 tip-off usually ends around 21:15-21:30. Overtime would push this later.

plan.weather_reason: The event is indoors and sold out. The day's 9 mm of rain falls outside the event window, with 0.0 mm in the hours around the game. Wind up to about 40 km/h may change how people make the last mile, not whether they come.
